scope: Proposition 3.5 (Three-mark sphere representation) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let hC be the whole-plane Gaussian free field (GFF) with circle average zero on ∂D, and put |z|+ = max{1, |z|}, GC(z, w) = log |z|+|w|+ |z − w| , Q = 2 γ + γ 2 . Define hL = hC + γGC(0, ·) + γGC(1, ·) − (2Q − γ) log | · |+, A = µhL (C). (3.3) Tilt the law of hL by the integrable strictly positive density A4/γ2−2/E[A4/γ2−2], and then set h = hL − γ−1 log A. (3.4) The result is the ordinary unit-area sphere with three independent area marks embedded at ∞, 0, 1. Resampling its three area marks and renormalizing gives the same law. In particular, on any bounded region avoiding 0, 1, its field modulo constants is locally mutually absolutely continuous with a whole-plane GFF modulo constants. Near 0, away from 1, the corresponding comparison field is hC − γ log | · |.
